objective: Reduce the complete repaired-coordinate cubic interaction space outcome-independently modulo degree two, measure the scalar target dimension relative to degree two, and express the two outcome targets in a deterministic cubic quotient basis without selecting a final decoder formula.

frozenPolynomialFamily.degree2: affine P/O plus every observed square-free pair of distinct active P/O bits
frozenPolynomialFamily.degree3: degree2 plus every observed square-free triple of distinct active P/O bits

outcomeIndependentReduction.method: Deterministic GF(2) column-priority elimination with all degree<=2 columns given pivot priority over cubic columns.
outcomeIndependentReduction.invariant: The number of retained cubic directions equals rank(DEGREE3)-rank(DEGREE2); individual retained triples are a gauge choice.

scalarTargetMeasurement: rank gain of y0 beyond the complete degree-2 span
rank gain of y1 beyond the complete degree-2 span
exactness of DEGREE2 plus the outcome-independent cubic quotient basis

discoveryGauge.purpose: After the cubic basis is frozen outcome-independently, solve y0/y1 in a deterministic zero-free-variable gauge and record which basis directions carry each target for motif discovery.

antiCircularity: Cubic basis selection uses only structural feature rows and degree ordering, never W/D/L labels.
Outcome columns are introduced only after the cubic quotient basis is frozen.
The deterministic target-coordinate gauge is explicitly outcome-fitted discovery evidence and may not be published as an invariant final formula.
No sealed EW-RS-059 holdout is solved or sampled during this experiment.
falsifiers: Any mismatch with the frozen degree-2 or degree-3 contradiction/rank-gain controls invalidates the run.
Any contradiction using degree two plus the reduced cubic quotient basis invalidates the basis reduction.
A joint target dimension greater than two rejects the retained two-output-direction hypothesis relative to degree two.
Failure to represent either target bit inside the reduced cubic basis indicates a reduction or harness error because full degree 3 is already exact.
nextIfTwoDimensional: Analyze the deterministic target-support cubic motifs across carriers and freeze an outcome-independent structural syndrome candidate before unsealing PRIMARY 3x6-k4.
nextIfNotTwoDimensional: Freeze the target-dimension result and revise the syndrome hypothesis before any formula selection.
interpretationGuards: Basis triple identities and fitted target supports are gauge-dependent discovery objects.
Invariant claims are quotient rank, target dimension, exactness, and later holdout behavior.
No Q-A/Q-F, standard-7x6, or universal theorem follows.
